stem: Choose the correct option and complete the sentence : Brazil has a coastline along the ____ Ocean.
solution: **(B)** Atlantic. Brazil lies in the eastern part of South America and its whole coastline faces the Atlantic Ocean: the North Atlantic along the northern coast near the mouth of the Amazon and the South Atlantic along the long eastern coast. Brazil does not touch the Pacific Ocean at all; it is separated from it by the countries of the Andes.

stem: Choose the correct option and complete the sentence : The river ____ is the second largest river system of India in terms of catchment area.
solution: **(B)** Godavari. The Godavari rises on the eastern slopes of the Western Ghats and flows east across the Peninsula into the Bay of Bengal, draining a very large part of the plateau. It is the second largest river system of India in terms of catchment area. The Narmada and the Tapi are west-flowing rivers with narrow rift-valley basins, and the Bhima is only a tributary of the Krishna.

stem: Choose the correct option and complete the sentence : The coastal region of Brazil receives ____ type of rainfall due to the obstruction by the escarpment.
solution: **(C)** Orographic. Parts of the Brazilian Highlands extend up to the coast and end in a steep escarpment. The escarpment obstructs the moisture-laden winds blowing from the sea, which are forced to rise, cool and condense, so the coastal region gets orographic (relief) rainfall. Beyond the highlands the effect of these winds is reduced and a rain-shadow region is formed.

subtopic: Types of Economy and National Income
stem: Choose the correct option and complete the sentence : India's per capita income is less than Brazil due to ____.
solution: **(D)** Massive population. Per capita income is the national income divided by the total population. India has a higher national income than Brazil, but India's population (about 121 crore) is many times Brazil's (about 19 crore), so dividing the national income by this huge population gives India a lower per capita income. Low national income cannot be the reason, because India's national income is in fact the larger one.

context: State whether the following sentences are right or wrong (any four) :
stem: State whether the sentence is right or wrong : The difference in temperatures are negligible towards the coastal regions near the equator in Brazil.
solution: Right. Near the equator the sun's rays are nearly vertical throughout the year, and on the coast the nearness of the sea keeps the climate mild. So in the coastal regions near the equator in Brazil the temperature does not vary much and the differences in temperature are negligible. Because of this the winds move vertically and the convergence zone of the trade winds is weak, so tropical cyclones rarely visit the coasts of Brazil.

solution: Wrong. The majority of Brazilians live within about 300 km of the eastern coastal plain, where agriculture and industries have developed, so it is the EASTERN part that is densely populated.

context: Give geographical reasons for the following (any two) :
stem: Give geographical reasons : Himalayan rivers are perennial in nature.
solution: Most of the major Himalayan rivers, such as the Indus, the Ganga and the Brahmaputra and their tributaries, originate from glaciers in the Himalayas. In summer, when the glaciers and the snow melt, the discharge of water in these rivers increases, so they keep flowing even in the dry season. During the monsoon they also receive heavy rainfall in their catchments and are often in flood. Since they get water from melting snow in summer and from rain in the monsoon, they carry water throughout the year. Hence the Himalayan rivers are perennial in nature.

subtopic: Types of Economy and National Income
context: Give geographical reasons for the following (any two) :
stem: Give geographical reasons : There is mixed economy in Brazil and India.
solution: In a mixed economy the public sector (owned and run by the government) and the private sector (owned and run by individuals and companies) work side by side. Both India and Brazil are developing economies. Heavy industries, power, mining, transport and other basic services need very large investment and give returns slowly, so the government undertakes them, while agriculture, trade, many industries and services are run by private enterprise. The public sector also works for welfare and balanced development, and the private sector adds efficiency and employment. Since both sectors operate together in both countries, there is a mixed economy in Brazil and India.

context: Give geographical reasons for the following (any two) :
stem: Give geographical reasons : Population is an important resource.
solution: Natural resources become useful only when people use them, so human beings are themselves a resource. A country's population provides the workers needed in agriculture, mining, industries, trade, transport and services, and it also provides the consumers who create a market for goods. The qualitative aspects of the population, such as literacy, health, skills, sex ratio and age structure, decide how productive it is: an educated, skilled and healthy population of working age raises production and income. Therefore the population is important for a nation's economic and social progress, and population is an important resource of any country.

context: Give geographical reasons for the following (any two) :
stem: Give geographical reasons : Sao Paulo has nucleated Settlement.
solution: Sao Paulo lies in the south-eastern part of Brazil. It has an extensive area of rich soil which is ideal for growing coffee, and a good supply of water. It has a large supply of natural minerals close by, such as iron ore, and a steady supply of energy. The south-eastern area also has a good transport system. These favourable conditions led to the growth of agriculture, industries and trade, which attracted a large number of people to live close together. This makes the Sao Paulo area a nucleated settlement.

subtopic: Purpose and Planning of a Field Visit
context: Answer the following questions in detail (any two) :
stem: What is field visit ? State its importance.
solution:
A field visit is a planned visit to a place, made under the guidance of teachers, to observe and study its geographical features directly. During a field visit students observe and record the relief, water bodies, vegetation, soil, agriculture, occupations, human settlements and settlement patterns of the region, collect information through questions to local people, photographs and notes, and finally write a report.

Importance of a field visit:
- Geographical concepts learnt in the classroom are seen and understood in reality, so learning becomes concrete and lasting.
- Students learn to observe carefully and to record what they see, for example the change in relief, vegetation and settlement types along a route.
- It shows the relation between man and environment, such as how relief, water and soil decide the crops, occupations and settlements of a region.
- Students learn skills such as reading maps on the spot, preparing a questionnaire, interviewing people, taking photographs and writing a report.
- It develops planning, teamwork, discipline and responsibility, and creates awareness about caring for the environment, for example by managing litter during the visit.

context: Answer the following questions in detail (any two) :
stem: Explain the importance of the Himalayas and the Indian Ocean with respect to the climate of India.
solution:
The Indian Ocean and the Himalayan ranges exert a great influence on the climate of India and on the origin of the monsoons.

Importance of the Himalayas:
- The Himalayas obstruct the very cold winds blowing from the north (Central Asia), so northern India does not become extremely cold in winter.
- The moisture-laden south-west monsoon winds moving towards the north are obstructed by the Himalayas. They are forced to rise and give orographic rainfall to the northern plains and the Himalayan region.
- The monsoon winds retreat from the Shiwalik and Himachal ranges of the Himalayas, so the Himalayas also mark the turning point from which the retreating monsoon begins.

Importance of the Indian Ocean:
- In summer, high temperatures create low pressure areas over the Punjab plains and the Thar desert, while a high pressure region forms over the Indian Ocean. The winds therefore blow from the Indian Ocean towards the mainland of India.
- These winds pick up moisture over the ocean and bring rainfall to India, heavily on the coasts because of the Western and Eastern Ghats, less on the leeward side.
- While retreating from the north-east towards the Indian Ocean, these winds bring rainfall again to some parts of the Peninsula (the retreating monsoon season).
- Nearness to the ocean also keeps the coastal regions moderate in temperature.

Thus the Himalayas and the Indian Ocean together give India its monsoon type of climate.

context: Answer the following questions in detail (any two) :
stem: Write in detail about the industries in Brazil.
solution:
Brazil is one of the world giants of mining, agriculture and manufacturing, and its industries have developed on the basis of its rich resources.

- Major industries: iron and steel production, automobile assembly, petroleum processing, production of chemicals and cement making are the major industries of Brazil.
- Technology-based industries have been the most dynamic in recent years, but they have not outpaced the traditional industries.
- Agro-based and traditional industries: food processing such as the sugar industry, and cotton textile, silk and woollen industries have developed well.
- Raw materials: the eastern part of Brazil is rich in minerals such as iron ore, manganese, nickel, copper, bauxite and tungsten, which support heavy industries.
- Location: most of the large industries are concentrated in the south and south-east, for example around Sao Paulo, where minerals, a steady energy supply, a good transport system and a large population are available. Sao Paulo has emerged as a major metropolitan and industrial area.
- The north-east is traditionally the poorest part of Brazil, but it is beginning to attract new investment, while the interior Amazon region has little industry because of dense forests and inaccessibility.

Thus industries in Brazil are diverse but unevenly distributed, concentrated mainly in the south-east.
